transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been having hallucinations lately. I keep seeing and hearing things that other people say aren't actually there, and it's getting really hard to cope with

Have you also had times when your mood was very depressed or unusually high and energetic around the same time as the hallucinations? If so, did the hallucinations ever happen when your mood felt normal?

Yes, I've had periods where I felt incredibly energetic and high, or really down and depressed, at the same time I was hallucinating. But there was also a time for about two or three weeks where I still heard and saw things even though my mood felt completely normal.
During the times you felt unusually high and energetic, did you need much less sleep and feel more talkative, impulsive, or grandiose than usual?

During those high-energy times, I definitely couldn't stop talking and made a lot of impulsive decisions, like spending money recklessly. I also felt incredibly powerful and special, like I had grand abilities. I don't really recall how my sleep patterns were back then, though.

Over the whole time you’ve been ill, have these mood episodes taken up most of the time, or have the hallucinations and other psychotic symptoms been present for long stretches even when mood symptoms were absent?

Yes, those high-energy mood episodes have definitely taken up the majority of the year and a half that I've been sick. However, there was still that period of about two weeks where the hallucinations and delusions continued even when my mood had completely leveled out.
Just to be clear, did the hallucinations and delusions continue for at least two full weeks when you were not depressed or unusually high at all?
Yes, that is absolutely correct. There was a period of at least two weeks where my mood felt completely stable and normal, but the hallucinations and delusions just kept happening.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent hallucinations and delusions, with prominent manic symptoms and depressive periods during the illness. Crucially, psychotic symptoms continued for at least two weeks in the absence of any mood episode, while mood episodes were present for the majority of the total illness duration. This pattern is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type.
